approvedDesign: Outside maintained PowerShell observer records QPC start/frequency before Python creation and observes actual final controller exit against that same fixed30s end.

Canonical outer WindowsScope atomically owns fixed E worker and nested installed launcher/jpackage descendants; existing E semantics retained but all allocations and final acceptance clipped to the shared end.

Independent outer watchdog stays armed through ordinary os._exit; fatal path uses original-self TerminateProcess, not borrowed Job handle. Outside process-death observation proves watchdog death; no false thread-join claim.
Separate helper/app source identities and retained account/startup/package preflight; no policy, application or provider activation change.
boundedImplementationChecks: Keep sole outer Job handle noninheritable and alive until complete outer retirement; avoid close-versus-watchdog handle races.
Use same native QPC domain/frequency with strict typed finite range/overflow/future/expired checks; no renewed30s timer or appended cleanup budget.

Reject late exit0/receipt, overflow, unclosed captures and any uncertain cleanup; outer observer must retain original process handle and use remaining time, not PID relookup or an unbounded final ReadToEnd/wait.
Start watchdog before scope/knownfolder/worker preparation; avoid adding unowned git/helper subprocesses for provenance. Bound actual helper-file hashes with independently retained source metadata.
Trust assumption is ordinary CPython/GIL and OS progress, not a hard OS scheduling/termination guarantee. Failed hard stop cannot certify descendant cleanup.

Before installed use, source-bound inert Windows controls must exercise successful/nested-descendant ownership, blocked worker/call cutoff, failure/late observations and controller termination. No account87/1314 rerun or provider payload in these controls.
scope: Architecture only; source implementation and actual Windows control results remain to be independently reviewed. No source edits/tests/native execution/API writes.
